researched.name: Swastika Infra Ltd
researched.reason: Reg 30 LOA from MSEDCL, Rs 615.76 cr including taxes, Bhandup Zone Maharashtra, 24 months, not a related party. Against a trailing year of sales - the one order ratio the 1,245-filing study found predictive - this is 1.22x FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 503.57 cr, or 1.04x after an assumed 18% GST; against market cap it is 0.86x, the ratio the study found predicts nothing. Read the 460-page RHP dated 17-Sep-2026 on BSE for the base business: revenue Rs 209.58 -> 350.76 -> 503.57 cr over FY24-26, PAT Rs 13.98 -> 27.45 -> 41.43 cr, EBITDA margin 11.31 -> 14.07%, order book Rs 391.39 -> 650.23 -> 687.44 cr, 96.87% of FY26 revenue from state DISCOMs. The board's own CA-certified FY27 working-capital projection (resolution 24-Aug-2026) inverts to an FY27 revenue assumption of about Rs 718 cr, +42.6%, with five line items agreeing - that is management guidance recovered by arithmetic, not an estimate of mine. Post-issue trailing PE 17.3x on 3,41,20,187 shares, FY27E 12.1x against Vikran 14.25x and Rajesh Power 9.62x. Three measured things hold it to medium: the 'first order filing' rarity the study rewards is an artifact of a six-day listing history (the RHP's own top-five table shows five large DISCOM wins between Oct-2023 and Jul-2026, which is the serial-bidder side of the study); working capital absorbed 2.54x EBITDA in FY25 and 99.7% in FY26, and the FY27 plan consumes the whole Rs 90 cr of IPO money earmarked for it; and contingent liabilities are Rs 272.68 cr of bank guarantees, about 7x PAT.

researched.name: IZMO Ltd
researched.reason: NOT PUBLISHED - the headline number is money IZMO PAYS, not revenue it receives. Opened the 07-Oct-2026 press release in full. The Rs 99.94 cr is the TOTAL OUTLAY of a five-year MeitY-sanctioned research programme (CPPICS Phase II / SPECTRA) at IIT Madras, of which MeitY contributes Rs 97.54 cr and izmo Microsystems Pvt Ltd commits Rs 2.40 cr 'cash and in-kind'. The instrument is a Memorandum of Understanding with IIT Madras for a packaging and industrialisation role - there is no order, no contract value and no revenue to IZMO anywhere in the document. Against that, the BSE detailed results show FY26 revenue of Rs 41.67 cr and FY26 PAT of Rs 0.13 cr, with FY25's Rs 24.43 cr PAT almost entirely other income (Rs 32.20 cr for the year, Rs 30.80 cr of it in a single quarter). So a Rs 1,335 cr market cap sits on Rs 41.67 cr of revenue (32x sales) and essentially no earnings - BSE's own header shows EPS -0.06 and PE -14,853. Nothing here clears the bar, and the Rs 99.94 cr must not be reported as an order.

researched.name: Silver Touch Technologies Ltd
researched.reason: NOT PUBLISHED - a real order, but in the weakest bucket the study measured, from a frequent announcer, on a rich multiple. Opened the filing: purchase order from ITI Ltd (Network Systems Unit, Bengaluru, a DoT PSU) for 80 high-performance enterprise servers with a 3-year warranty for an Indian Army deployment, Rs 35,63,18,292.20 inclusive of GST, supply in up to 3 lots within 6 months, won through a two-bid tender plus reverse auction. A separate 8-year AMC of Rs 14,04,07,208.04 is envisaged 'at a later date upon successful completion of the warranty period, if required' - a contingent future award, not part of today's order, so the 'Rs 49.67 cr aggregate over 11 years' the filing quotes should not be counted as intake. Against FY26 revenue of Rs 315.13 cr the Rs 35.63 cr gross is 11.3%, and about 9.6% after an assumed 18% GST - i.e. the under-10%-of-sales bucket, which reached 2x within two years only 21.4% of the time against 35.7% for the 25-50% bucket. On rarity it is the wrong side too: this is its THIRD order announcement in 15 days (22-Sep Gujarat Energy Ltd, 26-Sep Space Applications Centre/ISRO, 07-Oct ITI), three in the 240-day window read (announcements_status complete; the full two-year count is unmeasurable because BSE refuses date ranges over 12 months). And it is not cheap - BSE header PE 39.29 on EPS 3.44, PB 14.75 - while the stock is already down 28.0% in three months. Size, rarity and price all point the same way.

researched.name: Blue Cloud Softech Solutions Ltd
researched.reason: NOT PUBLISHED - today's filing is not new information, and the announcement pattern is the playbook's explicit skip. Opened the filing: it is a follow-up to a disclosure dated 25-Sep-2026, reporting that Global Impx Inc, USA - a wholly owned subsidiary - has COMMENCED DELIVERY of an AI-infrastructure engagement for IBM Cloud Inc at a fixed fee of US$15,500,000 (about Rs 147 cr), with work 'under way on requirement gathering and infrastructure assessment, the first phases of a 13-phase implementation plan'. The order was already announced twelve days earlier, so there is no new order today; what is new is that phase 1 of 13 has begun. Against FY26 revenue of Rs 637.02 cr the Rs 147 cr is 23.1% of a year's sales, just under the study's best bucket - but 79 announcements in 240 days (status complete) read as a press-release engine rather than an order book: a 'STRATEGIC PLAN TO INVEST UP TO US$1 BILLION IN NEXT-GENERATION AI-POWERED DATA CENTER BUSINESS' (09-Feb-2026), an LOI for a national ISP licence (18-Feb), MoUs with GCIB for Africa (28-Apr, 20-Aug) and Afro Mobile SARL, a five-year master services agreement (13-Jul) and multiple Hyderabad City Police work orders. There is also a structure worth understanding before anything is published: the company ACQUIRED Global Impx Inc - the entity receiving the IBM fee - from ConnectM Technology Solutions Inc (board approval 23-Feb-2026, press release 06-Apr-2026), and ConnectM Technology Solutions then appears as a Reg 29(1) acquirer of Blue Cloud shares on 24-Jun-2026, with AstraBridge Inc on 23-Jun-2026. The acquisition consideration was NOT read this run (those filings were not opened), so no figure for it is asserted. Promoter holding is only 38.44%, BSE header PE 36.29 on PB 18.64, and the stock is down 23.5% over a year despite the announcement flow. The trigger is a press release about a previously announced order; skipped.

note: Three lanes worked, one idea published. GOVERNMENT produced nothing and that is the correct answer: 52 PIB releases scanned by GitHub Actions at 18:56 IST, 0 kept, 0 unmapped, no theme added, nothing manufactured. COMMODITY produced nothing either, and the reason is worth recording because it was a close call: the strongest-strength groups are all driven by WPI for 2026-04 and trade for 2026-07 - evidence months old that has not moved in weeks - while the one genuinely fresh daily mover, ICE sugar at +11.1% on the week, dies at the Indian border: every Chinimandi ex-mill M/30 print is flat to MINUS 15.7% on the month, on deep series, because Indian sugar is set by MSP, release quotas and ethanol diversion rather than by ICE. AVADHSUGAR had shown up independently in the scan on 6.2x volume at the window high, which is exactly the confluence this lane hunts, and it was rejected on the Indian print rather than published on the global one. No Indian print anywhere in the panel moved more than 2.6% on the week, and that one sits on four readings and is not marked deep. FILINGS carried the day: 15 candidates, four names researched from their own primary documents, one published. The published idea - Swastika Infra, a Rs 615.76 cr MSEDCL LOA worth 1.22x a trailing year's sales on a Rs 717 cr market cap six trading days after listing - rests on a 460-page RHP read from BSE, and the single most useful thing in it was not a disclosure but an arithmetic recovery: the board's CA-certified FY27 working-capital projection, expressed in days of revenue, inverts to management's own FY27 revenue assumption of about Rs 718 cr (+42.6%), with five independent line items agreeing to within 2.6%. It is held to medium confidence, and the reason is the kind of honesty this page is for: the 'first order filing in two years' rarity that the 1,245-filing study rewards most is, here, an artifact of a six-day listing history - the RHP's own top-five table shows five large DISCOM wins between October 2023 and July 2026, which is the serial-bidder side of the study, not the rare-filer side. The three names NOT published are as much of the day's output as the one that was, and one of them is a number that should never reach a reader as an order: IZMO's 'Rs 99.94 crore MeitY programme' is a five-year research outlay of which MeitY pays Rs 97.54 cr and izmo Microsystems commits Rs 2.40 cr in cash and in kind - IZMO is a net PAYER under an MoU, on a Rs 1,335 cr market cap carrying Rs 41.67 cr of FY26 revenue and Rs 0.13 cr of FY26 PAT.
